what_happened.line: The Commission voted 5-0 to order Hickory Hills Landowners to remove gravel from the boat ramp within 30 days.
A motion to approve the 238 Fire Road 16 application as submitted failed 2-3, so the house, driveway and crossing were neither approved nor denied.
The Commission approved or issued determinations on several filings, including a garage on Flynn Road, a Bright Farms greenhouse and a Mopus Road driveway.
Hearings on 200 Island Road and 1672 Mass Ave were continued, and the Lake Shirley drawdown date request was continued two weeks.
The Commission declined the Chapter 61A right of first refusal at 360 Flat Hill Road, and members said the price was unknown and likely beyond its budget.

why_it_matters: The boat ramp order bears on public access to Hickory Hills' ramp when the water is drawn down.
The 238 Fire Road 16 project is still undecided, so the application will have to come back to the Commission.
Passing on the Flat Hill Road land means that parcel is not likely to be bought for conservation.
watch_next: 200 Island Road hearing continued to October 21, with a revised plan reducing the driveway in the 50-foot zone and showing the limit of work.
1672 Mass Ave hearing continued to November 4.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on nearly all votes and outcomes, mostly unanimous, with only street and name spellings differing. The main difference is attendance: our minutes list the conservation agent as present, but the official minutes say staff was absent due to a power outage. Our 5-0 and 4-0 tallies, the 2-3 on Fire Road 16, the Lake Shirley request, and the Flat Hill price do not appear in the official text.
